rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening letters may refer to verses mentioned in the preceding sura.
rows.anchor: أنها الآيات المتقدم ذكرها في السورة التي قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they refer to the verses of this sura, with تلك meaning these.
rows.anchor: الآيات التي في هذه السورة

rows.speaker: ابن بحر
rows.claim: Ibn Bahr takes the opening letters as signs of the Arabic Book.
rows.anchor: أن تلك الآيات إشارة إلى ما افتتحت به السورة من الحروف

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains the clear Book as making its lawful and unlawful matters clear.
rows.anchor: المبين حلاله وحرامه , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada understands the clear Book as making its guidance and right direction clear.
rows.anchor: المبين هداه ورشده , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: معاذ
rows.claim: Muadh says it clarifies the six letters absent from the tongues of non-Arabs.
rows.anchor: المبين للحروف التي سقطت من ألسن الأعاجم

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority understand that God sent down the Book as an Arabic Qur'an in the language of the Arabs.
rows.anchor: إنا أنزلنا الكتاب قرآنا عربيا بلسان العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rare interpretation takes the referent as Joseph's account, collected in Arabic and eloquently expressing its meanings.
rows.anchor: إنا أنزلنا خبر يوسف قرآنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best storytelling means giving the best explanation; a storyteller relates an account as it truly happened.
rows.anchor: أي نبين لك أحسن البيان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada say Joseph saw his brothers and parents prostrating, then referred to them as eleven stars, the sun, and the moon.
rows.anchor: أنه رأى إخوته وأبويه ساجدين له

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Most interpreters say he saw the eleven stars, sun, and moon prostrating; they signify his brothers, father, and mother.
rows.anchor: أنه رأى أحد عشر كوكبا والشمس والقمر ساجدين له

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj assigns the sun to his mother and the moon to his father because the sun is grammatically feminine and the moon masculine.
rows.anchor: الشمس أمه والقمر أبوه , لتأنيث الشمس

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Jabir reports that the Jewish questioner Bustana asked the Prophet for the stars' names; Gabriel supplied them, and the questioner affirmed the names.
rows.anchor: روى السدي عن عبد الرحمن بن سابط عن جابر قال : أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رجل من اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reported names are Jaryan, al-Tariq, al-Dhayyal, Dhu al-Katifayn, Qabis, al-Waththab, al-Amudan, al-Faliq, al-Musabbih, al-Duruh, Dhu al-Far, al-Diya, and al-Nur.
rows.anchor: والطارق والذيال وذو الكتفين وقابس والوثاب والعمودان والفليق والمصبح والضروح وذو الفرع والضياء

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the repeated phrase emphasizes the first sighting because a considerable interval separates the two clauses.
rows.anchor: تأكيدا للأول لبعد ما بينهما قاله الزجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation distinguishes seeing the celestial bodies in the first clause from seeing their prostration in the second.
rows.anchor: أن الأول رؤيته لهم والثاني رؤيته لسجودهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation takes their prostration as the familiar prayer prostration, performed in reverence rather than worship.
rows.anchor: أنه السجود المعهود في الصلاة إعظاما لا عبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Joseph saw them humbled and described their humility as prostration; a poetic line depicts hills prostrate under hooves.
rows.anchor: أنه رآهم خاضعين فجعل خضوعهم سجودا

none: The segment contains only a brace and no commentary text.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Joseph was seventeen when he had this dream.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنه كان له عند هذه الرؤيا سبع عشرة سنة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas dates the dream to Friday night, which was Laylat al-Qadr; Jacob feared the brothers' envy when Joseph told him.
rows.anchor: رأى هذه الرؤيا ليلة الجمعة وكانت ليلة القدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says Jacob first dismissed it as a night dream not to rely on, then privately warned Joseph not to tell his brothers lest they plot.
rows.anchor: يا بني هذه رؤيا الليل فلا يعول عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says the name Yusuf is foreign.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أنه اسم أعجمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view derives Yusuf from Arabic asaf, meaning sorrow.
rows.anchor: أنه عربي مشتق من الأسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says God chooses Joseph for his good character and constitution.
rows.anchor: أحدها : بحسن الخلق والخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view explains God's choosing Joseph as his refraining from revenge.
rows.anchor: الثاني : بترك الانتقام

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan interprets God's choosing Joseph as choosing him for prophethood.
rows.anchor: الثالث : بالنبوة , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets the interpretation of reports as the interpretation of dreams.
rows.anchor: أحدها : عبارة الرؤيا , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets it as knowledge and wisdom.
rows.anchor: الثاني : العلم والحكمة , قاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third meaning is the outcomes of affairs; a verse of poetry uses ta'wil for what comes before the day of separation.
rows.anchor: الثالث : عواقب الأمور , ومنه قول الشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says God completes His blessing by selecting Joseph for prophethood.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : باختيارك للنبوة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says the blessing is completed by elevating Joseph's standing and fulfilling his dream.
rows.anchor: الثاني : بإعلاء كلمتك وتحقيق رؤياك , قال مقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third possibility is that Joseph's brothers come to him and he blesses them after their mistreatment of him.
rows.anchor: أن أخرج إخوته إليه حتى أنعم عليهم بعد إساءتهم إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God completes the blessing on Jacob's family by placing prophethood among them.
rows.anchor: بأن جعل فيهم النبوة

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says God's blessing on Abraham was saving him from the fire and on Isaac was saving him from sacrifice.
rows.anchor: فنعمته على إبراهيم أن أنجاه من النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account takes the signs in Joseph's story as lessons for those who reflect.
rows.anchor: أنها عبر للمعتبرين . الثاني : زواجر للمتقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account takes them as warnings for the God-fearing.
rows.anchor: أنها عبر للمعتبرين . الثاني : زواجر للمتقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One lesson is the outcome God brings about after people wrong Joseph.
rows.anchor: ما أظهره الله تعالى فيه من عواقب البغي عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another lesson is that Joseph's dream proved true and its interpretation was correct.
rows.anchor: الثاني : صدق رؤياه وصحة تأويله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story shows Joseph restraining himself, mastering desire, avoiding sin, and fulfilling the trust.
rows.anchor: ضبط نفسه وقهر شهوته حتى سلم من المعصية وقام بحق الأمانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further lesson is relief after intense despair.
rows.anchor: الرابع : الفرج بعد شدة الإياس

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata says every grieving person who hears Surat Yusuf finds comfort in it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : ما سمع سورة يوسف محزون إلا استروح إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brother called Yusuf's brother is Benjamin; they were full brothers, and Jacob cared for them especially after their mother's death.
rows.anchor: وأخوه بنيامين وهما أخوان لأب وأم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's special care and strong love for Joseph caused the brothers' jealousy, which intensified after the dream.
rows.anchor: وكان شديد الحب ليوسف , فكان الحسد له أكثر

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Said ibn Jubayr defines the group as six or seven people.
rows.anchor: أحدها : أنها ستة أو سبعة , قاله سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid defines the group as ten to fifteen people.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أنها من عشرة إلى خمسة عشر , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada defines the group as ten to forty people.
rows.anchor: الثالث : من عشرة إلى أربعين , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
rows.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd takes the word to mean a group in general.
rows.anchor: الرابع : الجماعة , قاله عبد الرحمن بن زيد

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd reads their accusation as saying their father was mistaken in his judgment.
rows.anchor: أحدها : لفي خطأ من رأيه , قال ابن زيد

rows.speaker: ابن كامل
rows.claim: Ibn Kamil reads their accusation as saying their father acted unjustly.
rows.anchor: الثاني : لفي جور من فعله , قال ابن كامل

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: A report attributed to Ibn Jarir understands their phrase as referring to Jacob's manifest love.
rows.anchor: الثالث : لفي محبة ظاهرة , حكاه ابن جرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They called Jacob misguided because he favored the younger over the older, the few over the many, and those who did not care for his interests over those who did.
rows.anchor: لأنه فضل الصغير على الكبير

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: One group says the brothers were adults and believers, though not yet prophets, citing their request that Jacob seek forgiveness for them.
rows.anchor: واختلف فيهم هل كانوا حينئذ بالغين ؟ فذهب قوم إلى أنهم كانوا بالغين مؤمنين

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others say the brothers were minors, citing their request to take Joseph out to play and their later request for forgiveness after adulthood.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : بل كانوا غير بالغين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation of casting Joseph into a land is to expose him to wild beasts.
rows.anchor: اطرحوه أرضا لتأكله السباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is to put him far away from his father.
rows.anchor: الثاني : ليبعد عن أبيه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the brothers meant to become righteous in worldly affairs after removing Joseph.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أنهم أرادوا صلاح الدنيا لا صلاح الدين , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says they meant religious righteousness through repentance.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أنهم أرادوا صلاح الدين بالتوبة , قاله السدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third possibility is that they meant to set their affairs right by having their father treat them equally without preference.
rows.anchor: أنهم أرادوا صلاح الأحوال بتسوية أبيهم بينهم من غير أثرة ولا تفضيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage supports the acceptability of a murderer's repentance because God does not condemn their statement here.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا دليل على أن توبة القاتل مقبولة لأن الله تعالى لم ينكر هذا القول منهم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada identifies the brother who objected to killing Joseph as Reuben, the eldest brother and their maternal aunt's son.
rows.anchor: أحدها : أنه روبيل وهو أكبر إخوة يوسف وابن خالته , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies the objecting brother as Simeon.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أنه شمعون , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the objecting brother as Judah.
rows.anchor: الثالث : أنه يهوذا , قال السدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of the pit's hidden recess is its bottom and deepest part.
rows.anchor: يعني قعر الجب وأسفله

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi explains it as the darkness of the pit that hides whatever is inside; its opening was narrow and its bottom wide.
rows.anchor: ظلمة الجب التي تغيب عن الأبصار ما فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of the name is that Joseph's news disappeared in the pit.
rows.anchor: لأنه يغيب فيه خبره

rows.speaker: ابن أحمر
rows.claim: Ibn Ahmar's verse supports the explanation that a person's trace disappears into a hidden recess.
rows.anchor: لأنه يغيب فيه أثره , قال ابن أحمر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the well was a known well in Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: اسم بئر في بيت المقدس , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says jubb is a generic, unspecified well, a particular kind of well.
rows.anchor: بئر غير معينة , وإنما يختص بنوع من الآبار

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-Asha's verse uses jubb for a deep well, here described as eighty fathoms deep.
rows.anchor: لئن كنت في جب ثمانين قامة … ورقيت أسباب السماء بسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One definition of jubb is a large well, whether it contains water or not.
rows.anchor: ما عظم من الآبار سواء كان فيه ماء أو لم يكن

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines jubb as an unlined well, named for being cut from earth without further construction.
rows.anchor: أنه ما لا طي له من الآبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaltaqiṭ means to take; luqṭa is named for something lost and picked up.
rows.anchor: معنى يلتقطه يأخذه , ومنه اللقطة لأنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation of al-sayyara is travelers, named for their journeying.
rows.anchor: هم المسافرون سموا بذلك لأنهم يسيرون

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets al-sayyara as people passing along the road.
rows.anchor: هم مارة الطريق , قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets yartaʿ wa-yalʿab as having fun and playing.
rows.anchor: أحدها : نلهو ونلعب , قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada interprets the phrase as going about energetically and being active.
rows.anchor: الثاني : نسعى وننشط , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the brothers would keep watch over one another, protect one another, and play.
rows.anchor: الثالث : نتحارس فيحفظ بعضنا بعضا ونلهو , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets it as grazing and roaming; a line by al-Farazdaq uses the verb in this sense.
rows.anchor: الرابع : نرعى ونتصرف , قاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: ابن شجرة
rows.claim: Ibn Shajara interprets it as eating and enjoying ample food and drink, from ritʿa, abundance in eating and drinking.
rows.anchor: الخامس : نطعم ونتنعم مأخوذ من الرتعة وهي سعة المطعم والمشرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob did not object to their proposed play because they meant permissible play.
rows.anchor: ولم ينكر عليهم يعقوب عليه السلام اللعب لأنهم عنوا به ما كان مباحا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Jacob feared the brothers, called them wolves indirectly, and spoke of the wolf to accommodate them.
rows.anchor: أنه قال ذلك لخوفه منهم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says Jacob did not fear the brothers, since he would not have sent Joseph with them; wolves were the common danger in the wilderness.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني : ما خافهم عليه

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says Jacob feared the wolf because he had dreamed that one attacked Joseph.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي : بل رأى في منامه أن الذئب شد على يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation of God's inspiration to Joseph is that He instilled the message in him, as in the revelation to Moses' mother.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : يعني وألهمناه , كما قال تعالى

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Mujahid and Qatada say God revealed to Joseph while he was in the pit.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أن الله تعالى أوحى إليه وهو في الجب , قاله مجاهد وقتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says Joseph was told he would later meet his brothers and rebuke them, so this revelation came after he was put in the pit as reassurance of safety.
rows.anchor: أنه أوحى إليه أنه سيلقاهم ويوبخهم على ما صنعوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says Joseph was told what his brothers would do to him, so this revelation came before he was cast into the pit as a warning.
rows.anchor: أنه أوحى إليه بالذي يصنعون به

rows.speaker: قتادة وابن جريج
rows.claim: Qatada and Ibn Jurayj say the brothers did not realize that the boy was their brother Joseph.
rows.anchor: لا يشعرون بأنه أخوهم يوسف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid say they did not realize God had revealed prophethood to him.
rows.anchor: لا يشعرون بوحي الله تعالى له بالنبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caravan's water-drawer is the person who goes ahead to the water to draw for the group.
rows.anchor: وهو الذي يرد أمامهم الماء ليستقي لهم

rows.speaker: أصحاب التواريخ
rows.claim: Historical accounts name the water-drawer Malik ibn Dhu'ar ibn Hajar ibn Yaka ibn Lakhm.
rows.anchor: وذكر أصحاب التواريخ أنه مالك بن ذعر بن حجر بن يكه بن لخم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adla means to lower or let down the bucket to fill it; dala means to pull it up full.
rows.anchor: أي أرسلها ليملأها , يقال أدلاها إذا أرسل الدلو ليملأها

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Joseph caught hold of the bucket as it was lowered.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة : فتعلق يوسف عليه السلام بالدلو حين أرسلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The well was a known place in Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: والبئر ببيت المقدس معروف مكانها

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the water-drawer called out to the group with good news of a boy.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أنه ناداهم بالبشرى يبشرهم بغلام , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the water-drawer called one of the group, whose name was Bushra, to tell him about the boy.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أنه نادى أحدهم , كان اسمه بشرى فناداه باسمه يعلمه بالغلام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Joseph's brothers were nearby, claimed he was their slave, sold him, and concealed the sale price as their own merchandise.
rows.anchor: أحدها : أن إخوة يوسف كانوا بقرب الجب فلما رأوا الوارد قد أخرجه قالوا هذا عبدنا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the water-carriers secretly bought Joseph from their companions to keep him for themselves because he was cheap, agreeing to call him merchandise entrusted from the people at the water.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أن الواردين إلى الجب أسروا ابتياعه عن باقي أصحابهم ليكون بضاعة لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view says the buyers concealed the sale from the king so their companions would not learn of it, saying Joseph was entrusted merchandise.
rows.anchor: الثالث : أن الذين شروه أسروا بيعه على الملك حتى لا يعلم به أصحابهم

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak, as related by Juwaybir, says Joseph was thrown into the well at age six and remained there three days.
rows.anchor: أنه ألقي في الجب وهو ابن ست سنين

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says Joseph was thrown into the pit at age seventeen.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي : ألقي فيه وهو ابن سبع عشرة سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here shara means sold; Ibn Mufarrigh's verse uses the verb for selling a garment.
rows.anchor: معنى شروه أي باعوه , ومنه قول ابن مفرغ الحميري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The terms for selling and buying can describe either party, since each sells what is in his hand and buys what the other holds.
rows.anchor: واسم البيع والشراء يطلق على كل واحد من البائع والمشتري لأن كل واحد منهما بائع لما في يده مشتر لما في يد صاحبه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, and Mujahid say Joseph's brothers sold him to the caravan after claiming him as a slave.
rows.anchor: أنهم إخوته باعوه على السيارة حين أخرجوه من الجب فادعوه عبدا

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada say the caravan sold Joseph on behalf of the ruler of Egypt.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أن السيارة باعوه عن ملك مصر , قاله الحسن وقتادة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets bakhs as an unlawful price; Ibn Ata explains that the sale of a person who cannot be sold makes the price wrongful however large.
rows.anchor: قاله الضحاك , قال ابن عطاء : لأنهم أوقعوا البيع على نفس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada interprets bakhs as injustice.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أنه الظلم , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: مجاهد والشعبي
rows.claim: Mujahid and al-Sha'bi interpret bakhs as a small amount.
rows.anchor: الثالث : أنه القليل , قاله مجاهد والشعبي

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس وقتادة وعطية والسدي
rows.claim: One report says the price was twenty dirhams, divided between ten brothers at two each.
rows.anchor: أنه بيع بعشرين درهما اقتسموها وكانوا عشرة فأخذ كل واحد منهم درهمين

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says it was twenty-two dirhams, divided at two each among eleven brothers.
rows.anchor: الثاني : باثنين وعشرين درهما , كانوا أحد عشر فأخذ كل واحد درهمين

rows.speaker: عكرمة وابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ikrima and Ibn Ishaq say the price was forty dirhams.
rows.anchor: الثالث بأربعين درهما , قاله عكرمة وابن إسحاق

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the brothers bought shoes and sandals with the proceeds.
rows.anchor: وكان السدي يقول : اشتروا بها خفافا ونعالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says the dirhams were counted rather than weighed because the sellers cared little about him.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : معدودة غير موزونة لزهدهم فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says the sum was under forty dirhams, the minimum weight they measured, since their smallest weight was an uqiyya of forty dirhams.
rows.anchor: الثاني : لأنها كانت أقل من أربعين درهما , وكانوا لا يزنون أقل من أربعين درهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view takes those disinterested in Joseph to be his brothers, who had treated him as they did.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أنهم إخوة يوسف كانوا فيه من الزاهدين حين صنعوا به ما صنعوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes them to be the caravan members who sold him for so little.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أن السيارة كانوا فيه من الزاهدين حين باعوه بما باعوه به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reason for their disinterest is that they knew he was free and not legally purchasable.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : لعلمهم بأنه حر لا يبتاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reason is that they thought he was a slave but feared his owners would appear and reclaim him.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أنه كان عندهم عبدا فخافوا أن يظهر عليه مالكوه فيأخذوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation is that they discounted the price after testing Joseph and recognizing his merit; Ikrima says Joseph was freed after being sold.
rows.anchor: وفيه وجه ثالث : أنهم كانوا في ثمنه من الزاهدين لاختبارهم له وعلمهم بفضله , وقال عكرمة أعتق يوسف حين بيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account identifies the Egyptian purchaser as the Aziz, named Izfir ibn Rujayb.
rows.anchor: وهو العزيز ملكها واسمه إظفير بن رويجب

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq names the buyer's wife Ra'il daughter of Ra'ayil.
rows.anchor: واسمها راعيل بنت رعاييل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas names the buyer Qitfir, says he oversaw Egypt's treasuries, and names the king as al-Walid ibn al-Rayyan of the Amalekites.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : اسمه قطفير وكان على خزائن مصر

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says the seller to the king was Malik ibn Dhu'ar and that the price included twenty dinars, a robe, and two sandals.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل : وكان البائع له للملك مالك بن ذعر بعشرين دينارا وزاده حلة ونعلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation of akrimi mathwah is to make his lodging pleasant.
rows.anchor: فيه وجهان : أحدهما : أجملي منزلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is to raise his standing; a line by Kathir illustrates thawa as staying or dwelling.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أجلي منزلته , قال كثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hospitality meant giving Joseph good food, soft clothing, and a comfortable bed.
rows.anchor: وإكرام مثواه بطيب طعامه ولين لباسه وتوطئة مبيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He may benefit them financially if they sell him.
rows.anchor: قيل : في ثمنه إن بعناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, he may benefit them through service and acting on their behalf.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل : ينفعنا في الخدمة والنيابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking Joseph as a son would mean freeing and adopting him.
rows.anchor: إن أعتقناه وتبنيناه

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud names three people especially perceptive: the Aziz about Joseph, Shuayb's daughter about Moses, and Abu Bakr when appointing Umar.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الله بن مسعود : أحسن الناس في فراسة ثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation says God established Joseph in the land by bringing him out of the pit.
rows.anchor: فيه وجهان : أحدهما : بإخراجه من الجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says the king appointed Joseph to office.
rows.anchor: الثاني : باستخلاف الملك له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about teaching the interpretation of reports has the two interpretations already discussed earlier.
rows.anchor: قد ذكرنا في تأويله وجهين

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says God prevails over Joseph's affair until Joseph reaches the outcome God intended.
rows.anchor: غالب على أمر يوسف حتى يبلغ فيه ما أراده له , قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God prevails in His own affair: when He wills a thing, He says Be and it is.
rows.anchor: الثاني : غالب على أمر نفسه فيما يريده , أن يقول له كن فيكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reaching maturity means reaching the peak of strength and youthful vigor.
rows.anchor: يعني منتهى شدته وقوة شبابه

rows.speaker: الشعبي وربيعة وزيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Al-Sha'bi, Rabi'a, and Zayd ibn Aslam place the beginning of maturity at puberty.
rows.anchor: أحدها : ببلوغ الحلم , قاله الشعبي وربيعة وزيد بن أسلم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Said ibn Jubayr places the beginning of maturity at eighteen years.
rows.anchor: الثاني : ثماني عشرة سنة , قاله سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak place it at twenty years.
rows.anchor: الثالث : عشرون سنة , قاله ابن عباس والضحاك

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima places it at twenty-five years.
rows.anchor: الرابع : خمس وعشرون سنة , قاله عكرمة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi places it at thirty years.
rows.anchor: الخامس : ثلاثون سنة , قاله السدي

rows.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Al-Hasan, Mujahid, and Qatada place it at thirty-three years.
rows.anchor: السادس : ثلاث وثلاثون سنة . قاله الحسن ومجاهد وقتادة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says maturity ends at forty years.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أنه أربعون سنة , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: ابن جرير الطبري
rows.claim: A report attributed to Ibn Jarir al-Tabari says maturity ends at sixty years.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أنه ستون سنة , حكاه ابن جرير الطبري

rows.speaker: سحيم بن وثيل الرياحي
rows.claim: Suhaym ibn Wathil al-Riyahi's line speaks of a man of fifty whose strength is fully assembled, illustrating the term ashudd.
rows.anchor: أخو خمسين مجتمع أشدي

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says Joseph reached maturity at twenty.
rows.anchor: عشرون سنة , قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says Joseph reached maturity at thirty.
rows.anchor: الثاني : ثلاثون سنة , وهو قول مجاهد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets the judgment given to Joseph as intellect.
rows.anchor: أحدها : العقل , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation of the judgment is judging people.
rows.anchor: الثاني : الحكم على الناس . الثالث : الحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third interpretation is wisdom in one's actions.
rows.anchor: الثالث : الحكمة في أفعاله . الرابع : القرآن

rows.speaker: سفيان
rows.claim: Sufyan interprets the judgment as the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: الرابع : القرآن , قاله سفيان

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi interprets the judgment as prophethood.
rows.anchor: الخامس : النبوة , قاله السدي

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets the knowledge given to Joseph as jurisprudence.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : الفقه , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن أبي نجيح
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Najih interprets the knowledge as prophethood.
rows.anchor: الثاني : النبوة , قاله ابن أبي نجيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third possibility is that the knowledge was skill in interpreting dreams.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل وجها ثالثا : أنه العلم بتأويل الرؤيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation of the righteous rewarded here is those who obey.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : المطيعين . الثاني : المهتدين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the righteous as those who are rightly guided.
rows.anchor: الثاني : المهتدين , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wise person acts on what he knows, whereas a learned person may possess knowledge without acting on it.
rows.anchor: والفرق بين الحكيم والعالم أن الحكيم هو العامل بعلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The woman was Ra'il, wife of the Aziz Izfir.
rows.anchor: وهي راعيل امرأة العزيز إظفير

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the woman's name was Zulaikha.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك : وكان اسمها زليخا

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Izfir was unable to have intercourse with women and his wife was beautiful; Joseph had unsurpassed beauty.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحاق : وكان إظفير فيما يحكى لنا رجلا لا يأتي النساء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Joseph and Eve each received half of the world's beauty.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : اقتسم يوسف وحواء الحسن نصفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation of locking the doors is that she repeatedly locked them.
rows.anchor: فيه وجهان : أحدهما : بتكثير الأغلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that she fastened many bolts or locks.
rows.anchor: وغلقت الأبواب } فيه وجهان : أحدهما : بتكثير الأغلاق . الثاني : بكثرة الإيثاق

rows.speaker: عكرمة وأبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
rows.claim: Ikrima and Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami take hayta laka to mean I have prepared myself for you; this explains the reading with kasra and no hamza.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : معناه تهيأت لك , قاله عكرمة

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet's line uses hayta to witness the meaning I have prepared myself.
rows.anchor: لو كان معنيا بها لهيتا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada interpret hayta laka as come here.
rows.anchor: الثاني : هلم لك , قاله ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
rows.claim: Abu Amr ibn al-Ala cites a poem addressing the Commander of the Faithful and Iraq with hayt as an invitation to come.
rows.anchor: وأنشد أبو عمرو بن العلاء : أبلغ أمير المؤمنين أخا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The come-here interpretation corresponds to the reading with an open ha and is the more correct and eloquent reading.
rows.anchor: وهذا تأويل من قرأ هيت لك بفتح الهاء وهي أصح وأفصح

rows.speaker: طرفة بن العبد
rows.claim: Tarafa ibn al-Abd's verse uses hayta as a call to come.
rows.anchor: قال طرفة بن العبد : ليس قومي بالأبعدين إذا ما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Atiyya's report, says hayta laka is a Coptic phrase meaning come here.
rows.anchor: فحكى عطية عن ابن عباس أن

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says hayta laka is Arabic and means come here.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد بل هي كلمة عربية هذا معناها

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the phrase is Syriac.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن : هي كلمة سريانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maadh Allah means I seek refuge in God.
rows.anchor: أي أعوذ بالله

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj understands my lord as God: God treated me well, so I will not disobey Him.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : إن الله ربي أحسن مثواي فلا أعصيه , قاله الزجاج

rows.speaker: مجاهد وابن إسحاق والسدي
rows.claim: Mujahid, Ibn Ishaq, and al-Suddi understand my lord as the Aziz, Joseph's master, who treated him well; Joseph would not betray him.
rows.anchor: قاله مجاهد وابن إسحاق والسدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation says the woman's desire for Joseph was sexual desire.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أنه كان هم شهوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says she reclined and prepared herself for intercourse with him.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أنها استلقت له وتهيأت لمواقعته

rows.speaker: بعض المتأخرين
rows.claim: Some later scholars say Joseph's desire was to strike her when she solicited him, not to have intercourse.
rows.anchor: أنه هم بها أن يضربها حين راودته عن نفسه

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub treats the woman's clause as complete and reads Joseph's clause as saying he would have desired her had he not seen his Lord's proof.
rows.anchor: أن قوله ولقد همت به كلام تام قد انتهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation contrasts her sexual desire with Joseph's desire for chastity.
rows.anchor: الثالث : أن همها كان شهوة , وهمه كان عفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says Joseph only weighed action against restraint; unacted inner thought carries no blame, since hamm begins as inward speech and becomes action only when it appears.
rows.anchor: الرابع : أن همه بها لم يكن عزما وإرادة وإنما كان تمثيلا بين الفعل والترك

rows.speaker: جميل
rows.claim: Jamil's line about Buthayna illustrates hamm as an inward thought or intention.
rows.anchor: هممت بهم من بثينة لو بدا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan interprets Joseph's desire as the natural stirring of men's desire for women, though he mastered it.
rows.anchor: حركة الطباع التي في قلوب الرجال من شهوة النساء وإن كان قاهرا له وهو معنى قول الحسن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Joseph desired intercourse and resolved on it, loosening his waist-wrapper and sitting between her legs as a man sits with a woman; this was the majority exegetes' view.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : وحل الهميان يعني السراويل وجلس بين رجليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of such a sin among prophets is that God tests them so remembering the sin makes them cautious and diligent rather than relying on pardon and mercy.
rows.anchor: أحدها : أن كل نبي ابتلاه الله بخطيئة إنما ابتلاء ليكون من الله تعالى على وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation is that God tests them so they recognize His favor in overlooking their sin and not punishing them in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أن الله تعالى ابتلاهم بذلك ليعرفهم موقع نعمته عليهم بصفحه عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation is that they become examples who encourage sinners to hope in God's mercy and not despair of pardon when they repent.
rows.anchor: الثالث : أنه ابتلاهم بذلك ليجعلهم أئمة لأهل الذنوب في رجاء رحمة الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the proof was a divine warning: Son of Jacob, will you commit adultery and become like a bird that loses its feathers and cannot fly?
rows.anchor: أحدها : أن برهان ربه الذي رآه أن نودي بالنهي عن مواقعة الخطيئة

rows.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد والحسن وسعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Qatada, Mujahid, al-Hasan, and Said ibn Jubayr say Joseph saw Jacob's image asking whether he would commit the deeds of fools despite being written among the prophets.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أنه رأى صورة يعقوب وهو يقول : يا يوسف أتهم بفعل السفهاء

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid adds that each of Jacob's sons except Joseph had twelve sons, while Joseph had only two, and says Joseph's desire reduced his offspring.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد : فولد لكل واحد من أولاد يعقوب اثنا عشر ذكرا إلا يوسف

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Kab al-Qurazi says the proof was God's warning against adultery, seen by Joseph as the inscription of Qur'an 17:32 on a wall.
rows.anchor: الثالث : أن البرهان الذي رآه ما أوعد الله تعالى على الزنى

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq identifies the proof as Joseph's master, the Aziz Izfir.
rows.anchor: الملك إظفير سيده , قاله ابن إسحاق

rows.speaker: ابن بحر
rows.claim: Ibn Bahr says the proof was the inherited moral discipline of Joseph's forefathers: chastity, purity, and avoidance of corruption and betrayal.
rows.anchor: الخامس : أن البرهان الذي رآه هو ما آتاه الله تعالى من آداب آبائه

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says Joseph saw a curtain hiding her idol; when she said she was ashamed before it, he said he had more reason to be ashamed before his God.
rows.anchor: السادس : أن البرهان الذي رآه أنه لما همت به وهم بها رأى سترا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation takes the evil to mean desire and the indecency to mean intercourse.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أن السوء الشهوة , والفحشاء المباشرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the evil to mean punishment by the Aziz and the indecency to mean adultery.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أن السوء عقوبة الملك العزيز . والفحشاء مواقعة الزنى

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Ibn Amir read mukhlasin with a kasra on the lam, meaning those who sincerely obey God.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وابن عامر المخلصين بكسر اللام

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The remaining readers use a fatha on the lam, meaning those whom God selected for His message.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بفتح اللام , وتأويلها الذين أخلصهم الله برسالته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph had both qualities: sincere obedience to God and selection for God's message.
rows.anchor: وقد كان يوسف عليه السلام بهاتين الصفتين لأنه كان مخلصا في طاعة الله تعالى
